newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling shaky, cable seen testing $1.60.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling shaky, cable seen testing $1.60.

text.p: Sterling is vulnerable to further losses after skidding through a series of support levels against the dollar and the mark in European morning trading, technical analysts said.
Cable's drop through $1.62 and then $1.6110 now threatens a test of psychological support at $1.60, while sterling/mark is vulnerable to a tumble further towards 3.00 marks, they said.
"Cable had a bearish outside day yesterday and the impulsive breakdown from 1.6860 still dominates here," said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America.
Sterling fell two cents and three pfennigs in early trade.
At 0850 GMT sterling was at $1.6046/56, down from $1.6262/72 in late European trading on Tuesday. The pound sank to its lowest level since last March at $1.6005 in early trade.
A drop below $1.60 would expose the pound to further downside towards critical medium-term support at the $1.5860 March low, said Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase.
While there is a chance of a sharp rebound from $1.60, upticks are now favoured to be sold, with resistance at $1.61 ahead of the former key support at $1.62.
Cable's weakness dragged sterling/mark down within a whisker of support at 3.02 marks. It was at 3.0240/50 against 3.0546/56.

Analysts said selling into upmoves was favoured so long as sterling stays below Tuesday's high at 3.0633. Stannard said sterling's short-term upside momentum had been eliminated by its move below 3.03.
"But it has to decline below 3.0141 to trigger an Elliott sell signal, putting 2.9910 under pressure," he said. Below 2.9910 would signal another tumble to 2.9740, possibly 2.9555.

The focus is on the outcome of the two-day Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting which starts today. A Reuter survey said 16 out of 23 economists surveyed expected rates to rise by 25 basis points from 6.75 percent.
